headline: Ward 7's top rankings share the podium with peers, but its worst rankings stand alone.
summary:
Ward 7's six best rankings are less singular than 'first in the city' sounds. Take traffic proximity, the No. 1 spot on the Chicago Environmental Justice Index, which measures nearby annual traffic volume. Four other wards finish inside two points of it. The same pattern holds across the rest of the ward's top six, the other pollution-exposure measures and the cheap rent that rounds out the list, each with three to five other wards bunched close behind. A gap that small usually means several wards are effectively tied for the top spot.

The worst six rankings tell a different story about company. Four of them, including long commutes and packaged liquor licenses, have exactly one other ward within two points of Ward 7's score, the tightest margin the site tracks. One more has two. Only the restaurant count keeps closer company, with three other wards nearby. The long commute figure puts 41 percent of workers here on the road 45 minutes or more each way, the highest share in the city, and only one other ward comes close. Mostly, Ward 7 sits alone at the bottom of a curve the rest of the city clears easily.
reading_the_rankings: The restaurant ranking is the one most likely to mislead. Ward 7 finishes 50th out of 50, but the count behind it comes from ZIP code areas rather than ward boundaries, cut however the ZIP lines happen to fall, and the source itself calls the result low confidence. It measures a rough retail footprint for that patch of the city more than an exact count within Ward 7's own lines. Packaged liquor licenses and the major chain restaurant share carry a different problem. Both come from a ward field the city recorded before the 2023 remap, so part of what's being counted still reflects the ward's old shape. All three numbers probably point the same direction, that Ward 7 has very little retail food and drink activity, but the exact rank each lands on is shakier than the number implies.

news.headline: Advocate Health Breaks Ground On Hospital At South Chicago Lakefront Megadevelopment Site
news.note: Advocate Health broke ground on a smaller replacement for Trinity Hospital at 8000 S. DuSable Lake Shore Drive, part of a lakefront megadevelopment set to open in 2029.

news.headline: Steel Slag Meets Prairie at Chicago's Marian Byrnes Park, See This Natural Wonder in an Unnatural Setting
news.note: The Chicago Park District added a boardwalk, overlook, and picnic area to the 140-acre natural area in Jeffery Manor, built partly on old steel slag dumping grounds.

news.headline: Artifacts Of Louis Sullivan Building, Demolished In The '50s, Are Protecting South Shore's Lakefront
news.note: Carved limestone remnants of architect Louis Sullivan's demolished Walker Warehouse were found reused as lakefront revetment stone near Rainbow Beach.
